question.problem: Find the equation of the line that passes through the point $(6,4)$ and is parallel to $3x-y=7.$
question.worked_solution:
Since parallel lines have equal slopes, the slope of the new line should be equal to the slope of the line $3x-y=7.$ 

To find the slope of the line $3x-y=7,$ we convert the equation to slope-intercept form:

$$
\begin{aligned}3x-y & =7 \\ y & =3x-7\end{aligned}
$$

From the slope-intercept form, we can tell that the slope of the line is $3.$

So, we want a line with the slope $3$ that passes through the point $(6,4).$ Using point-slope form and simplifying, we obtain the equation of the line:

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =m(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-4 & =3(x-6) \\ y-4 & =3x-18 \\ y & =3x-14\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we write this equation in standard form.

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =3x-14 \\ -3x+y & =-14 \\ 3x-y & =14\end{aligned}
$$
